tldr: FlowBench is introduced as the first comprehensive benchmark for workflow-guided planning in LLM-based agents, evaluating agents across 51 scenarios in 6 domains with workflow knowledge in text, code, and flowchart formats. The results show that current LLMs, even GPT-4o, struggle with satisfactory planning, and flowcharts achieve the best overall trade-off among workflow formats.
contributions: First systematic formalization of different workflow knowledge representation formats (text, code, flowchart)
Construction of FlowBench, the first comprehensive benchmark for workflow-guided agent planning covering 51 scenarios across 6 domains and 22 roles
A holistic multi-tiered evaluation framework with static turn-level and dynamic session-level assessments
methods: The authors formalize three workflow knowledge formats: natural language text, Python pseudo-code, and Markdown Mermaid flowcharts. They construct FlowBench through a three-phase pipeline: task collection from 6 real-world domains (Customer Service, Personal Assistant, E-tailing Recommendation, Travel & Transportation, Logistics Solutions, and RPA), workflow organization with human-verified knowledge documents converted via GPT-4 into multiple formats, and interactive session generation using collaborative human-LLM annotation. A multi-tiered evaluation framework is designed comprising static turn-level evaluation (comparing predicted actions against ground truth) and simulated session-level evaluation (using a GPT-4-based user simulator for sequential planning).
results: GPT-4o achieves only 43.2% and 40.9% success rates on certain tasks. Workflow knowledge incorporation significantly improves planning at both turn and session levels. Flowchart format achieves the best overall performance, with notable advantages of 6.4%, 6.5%, and 5.6% F1 score for tool invocation across different LLMs in static turn-level evaluation. Code format is less effective on weaker LLMs due to complex symbolic expressions, while text format performs consistently. Cross-scenario transitions cause performance decline. Workflow knowledge plays a more significant role in expertise-demanding domains like RPA, E-tailing Recommendation, and Travel.
limitations: Workflow knowledge effectiveness varies by format and LLM capability; code format underperforms on weaker LLMs. Cross-scenario evaluation shows discernible decline compared to single-scenario. The benchmark itself presents profound challenges indicating current LLM-agent designs need considerable improvement.
